status_summary: No DHS directive or program reinvigorating or expanding enforcement against Chinese e-commerce sellers, shippers or warehouse operators over counterfeit goods was found. A trade-press report dated 2026-04-07 on CBP's fiscal year 2025 figures says intellectual property seizures rose to 25,079 from 20,516 in fiscal year 2024 (22.2 percent), with a retail value of about 7.4 billion dollars against 5.5 billion dollars; CBP lists a fiscal year 2025 seizure statistics report, whose China and e-commerce breakdown was not read. The suspension of duty-free de minimis treatment, tracked in c26-03, subjects low-value parcels to formal entry and is context only.
title: Expand DHS enforcement against Chinese e-commerce sellers and shippers of counterfeits
uncertainties: Checked systematically on 2026-10-18. (1) Federal Register API: the researcher's CBP-filtered query on counterfeit e-commerce shippers returned four documents (a low-value shipments proposed rule of 2026-10-08, two de minimis suspension rules of 2026-06-24 and an advance cargo data rule), and a reviewer rerun on counterfeit, intellectual property, e-commerce and China returned three of the same CBP documents; none targets Chinese sellers, shippers or warehouse operators over counterfeits, and the de minimis items are tracked in c26-03. (2) Unified Agenda: item listings could not be reached and the Federal Register fallback was used. (3) congress.gov and govinfo: H.R. 708, passed by the House on 2025-03-10 and referred to a Senate committee on 2025-03-11, would set up a DHS working group that examines DHS efforts against CCP trade practices, listing trafficking in counterfeit and pirated goods among them, with annual reports; it does not mention e-commerce sellers or warehouses and does not itself expand enforcement, so it is treated as related rather than qualifying. (4) Agency pages: CBP national media releases showed no item on e-commerce sellers; dhs.gov was unreachable and the CBP FY2025 seizure statistics report, including any China or e-commerce breakdown, was not read. (5) News: one search found a 2026-06-15 report of a local CBP counterfeit seizure operation with no new policy. The FY2025 seizure figures in status_summary rest on one trade-press report. A rise in seizures does not show a policy change or a China focus. A reader who counts the de minimis suspension as an expanded crackdown on e-commerce shipments could stage the record in_progress, but that action is tariff policy tracked in c26-03.
